issues.legal_issue: The market value of acquired land must be assessed on the evidentiary record rather than adopted from an earlier award whose basis is not established.
material_facts: The acquisition concerned 20.40 acres of land for a dam.
The reference court relied on an award concerning land in a neighbouring village, but the judgments did not discuss the basis for that award or the relevant value of the land.
The land was admitted to be Class I wet-crop land, and there was no acceptable material about differences in land quality.
The Supreme Court treated all the land as Class I and fixed the market value at Rs. 6,000 per acre.
issues.conclusion: The market value was fixed at Rs. 6,000 per acre, with all the acquired land treated as Class I land.
issues.legal_principle: A prior award for land in a neighbouring village cannot, by itself, justify the valuation where its basis and relevance are not established in the record. Valuation must be determined from the available material and the totality of the circumstances. No earlier case was cited on this valuation issue.

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning compensation for acquired land.
predicates.prior_award_basis_is_undiscussed: The court below relied on an earlier award without discussing its basis or its relevance to the land being valued.
predicates.land_quality_evidence_is_unacceptable: The record contains no acceptable material establishing differences in the quality of the acquired land.

issues.definition: When a compensation appeal relies on an unexplained earlier award and acceptable evidence of land-quality differences is absent, the market value is fixed by an assessment supported by the record.

issues.legal_issue: A tank or well used to supply water for cultivating acquired land does not receive a separate valuation in addition to the land.
material_facts: The reference court awarded a separate sum for a tank and well.
The Court stated that no separate value could be granted for a tank and well when their water was used to cultivate the land.
issues.conclusion: The separate award of Rs. 1,69,890 for the tank and well was disallowed.
issues.legal_principle: Where water from a tank or well is used to cultivate the land, a separate value for those irrigation sources is not payable. The Court relied on O. Janardhan Reddy & Ors. v. Spl. Dy. Collector, L.A. Unit-IV, LMD, Karimnagar, A.P. & Ors., (1994) 6 SCC 456.

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning compensation for acquired land.
predicates.irrigation_asset_water_is_used_for_culti: Water from a tank or well is used to cultivate the acquired land.

issues.definition: In a land-compensation appeal, when a tank or well supplies water for cultivation, separate compensation for that irrigation asset is not awarded.

issues.legal_issue: An additional amount previously awarded under the additional-compensation provision was illegal because the Collector had made the award before that amount was granted.
material_facts: The Collector made the award on November 16, 1977.
The reference court granted an additional amount under Section 23(1-A) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
The Supreme Court held that, given the date of the Collector's award, granting that additional amount was illegal and set it aside.
issues.conclusion: The additional amount of Rs. 1,16,000 awarded under Section 23(1-A) was set aside as illegal.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that the Section 23(1-A) amount granted in this case was illegal because the Collector's award had been made on November 16, 1977. The Court did not cite an earlier case for this ruling.

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning compensation for acquired land.
predicates.collector_award_preceded_the_later_addit: The Collector made the compensation award before the additional amount was granted in the subsequent proceedings.

issues.definition: When a compensation appeal concerns a later additional amount granted after the Collector's award, that later amount is set aside.

issues.legal_issue: Claimants receiving enhanced compensation are entitled to interest, solatium, and an additional amount calculated on the market value as directed by the Court.
material_facts: The claimants obtained enhanced compensation for the acquired land.
Possession had been taken, and the notification under Section 4(1) had been published before the Collector made the award.
The Court directed interest on enhanced compensation, solatium on enhanced compensation, and an additional amount on market value, each calculated over the periods specified in its order.
issues.conclusion: The claimants were awarded interest on enhanced compensation at 9% for the first year from possession and 15% thereafter until deposit; solatium at 30% on enhanced compensation until deposit; and an additional amount at 12% on market value from publication of the notification until the Collector's award or taking of possession, whichever was earlier.
issues.legal_principle: The Court ordered interest and solatium on the enhanced compensation and an additional amount on market value, using the possession date, notification date, Collector's award date, and deposit date specified in its order. Section 4(1) and Section 23(1-A) are mentioned in the judgment in connection with the notification and additional amount. No earlier case was cited for these directions; the judgment does not identify a statutory provision for the interest or solatium directions.

predicates.enhanced_compensation_is_awarded: The court increases the compensation payable for the acquired land.
predicates.possession_was_taken: Possession of the acquired land was taken.

issues.definition: When an acquisition-compensation appeal results in enhanced compensation for land of which possession was taken, the claimants receive interest, solatium, and an additional amount on market value.
